title: BACE: Technical Skills & Applications - Technical Skills and Applications - Spectroscopy & Chromatography
subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: According to the Beer-Lambert Law ($A = \epsilon c l$), absorbance ($A​$) is directly proportional to:
options: Concentration of the solute and path length.
questions.explain: The Beer-Lambert law states $A = \epsilon c l$, where $c​$ is concentration and $l​$ is path length.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: A DNA sample has an $A_{260}$ of 1.0 and an $A_{280}$ of 0.5. What is the $A_{260}/A_{280}$ ratio, and what does it indicate about purity?
options: Ratio = 0.5; Sample is contaminated with protein.
Ratio = 2.0; Sample is likely pure DNA.
Ratio = 2.0; Sample is contaminated with RNA.
questions.explain: Ratio $= 1.0 / 0.5 = 2.0$. Pure DNA usually has a ratio of $\approx 1.8$. A ratio of 2.0 is often seen with pure RNA or very pure DNA (depending on buffer). A ratio $<1.6$ indicates protein contamination.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: In Size Exclusion Chromatography (SEC), which molecules elute first?
options: Small molecules, because they enter the pores of the beads.
Large molecules, because they are excluded from the pores and travel the shortest path.
questions.explain: Large molecules cannot enter the porous beads; they flow around them (excluded) and elute first. Small molecules get trapped in the pores and elute later.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: Which type of chromatography separates proteins based on their net charge?
questions.explain: Ion exchange uses charged beads (anion or cation exchange) to bind proteins of opposite charge. Elution is achieved by changing salt concentration or pH.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: In Affinity Chromatography used for purifying His-tagged recombinant proteins, what ligand is typically immobilized on the beads?
questions.explain: Histidine tags (His-tags) have a high affinity for divalent metal ions like Nickel ($Ni^{2+}$), used in IMAC (Immobilized Metal Affinity Chromatography).
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: When quantifying protein concentration using the Bradford Assay, the shift in Coomassie Blue absorbance maximum occurs at which wavelength?
questions.explain: The Bradford reagent shifts from brown/red to blue upon binding protein, with a maximum absorbance at 595 nm.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: What is the 'void volume' ($V_0$) in a chromatography column?
options: The total volume of the column bed.
The volume of the mobile phase outside the beads.
The volume inside the pores of the beads.
The volume of the sample loaded.
questions.explain: The void volume is the volume of buffer required to pass through the column between the beads (interstitial space) before molecules that do not interact with the beads (excluded molecules) begin to elute.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: In High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC), what is the main factor providing higher resolution compared to traditional column chromatography?
options: High pressure forcing solvent through very small particles.
questions.explain: HPLC uses pumps to force solvent at high pressure through columns packed with very fine particles, drastically increasing surface area and resolution.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: You have a mixture of Protein A (positively charged) and Protein B (negatively charged) at pH 7. Which column would capture Protein B?
questions.explain: Protein B is negatively charged (anion). It will bind to positive charges. An Anion Exchange column contains positively charged beads.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: Which nanodrop result warns of potential phenol or guanidine contamination in a nucleic acid sample?
questions.explain: The $A_{260}/A_{230}$ ratio measures contamination by organic compounds like phenol, guanidine, or carbohydrates, which absorb near 230 nm. A pure sample usually has a ratio of 2.0–2.2. Lower values indicate contamination.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications
